m.x: The first edge of the threshold.This contains the lowest value for each channel.
The second edge of the threshold.This contains the highest value for each channel.If it is the same as the first edge, the threshold is a single value.

Whether each channel is inverted. When a channel is inverted, itsoutput is flipped so that values that would normally output 0 insteadoutput 1, and vice versa. This applies per-channel to the RGBAcomponents of the threshold result.
Toggle this boolean to enable or disable this filter,without removing it from and re-adding it to the Camera's filter list.

If `true`, this filter will be permitted to draw to the base texture.This can be unwanted if, for example, the filter doesn't actuallydraw anything.This is an internal flag used by the renderer.You should not modify this value directly.
A reference to the Camera that owns this filter.

The padding currently being used by this filter.This is read during rendering via `getPadding`, and may be updated by subclass implementations.It is necessary for filters being used in an external list.You should not modify this value directly.

Whether this filter controller will be destroyed when the FilterListthat owns it is destroyed. If you enable this, you must ensure thatyou clean up the filter controller at an appropriate time.This allows you to reuse a controller for multiple objects;this is not recommended unless you know what you're doing.It tends to work best with external filters.
Padding override. This is on by default. If this is set,the filter will use this padding instead of calculating it.Prefer using `setPaddingOverride` instead of modifying this directly.
The ID of the RenderNode that this filter uses.

Set the edges of the threshold.If the second edge is not provided, it will be set to the first edge.This ensures that the first edge is not greater than the second edge.It may swap channels between edges to ensure this.

p.x: The first edge of the threshold. This may be an array of the RGBA channels, or a single number to apply to all 4 channels.
The second edge of the threshold. This may be an array of the RGBA channels, or a single number to apply to all 4 channels.

m.x: Sets the invert state for each channel of the threshold filter.When a channel is inverted, its output is flipped: pixels that wouldoutput 0 instead output 1, and vice versa. This can be used to createnegative or reversed threshold effects per channel.If `invert` is not provided, all channels default to `false`.

p.x: Whether each channel is inverted. This may be an array of the RGBA channels, or a single boolean to apply to all 4 channels.

m.x: Destroys this Controller and nulls any references it holds.

Returns the raw padding required for this filter.This is typically not what you want to call; use `getPaddingCeil` instead.Values from this method are not rounded, which can cause quality loss.Override this method when creating a Filter that requires extra room,e.g. a blur or glow effect.

r.x: The padding required by this filter.

m.x: Returns the rounded padding required for this filter.Most filters don't need extra padding,but some may sample beyond the texture boundaries, such as a blur or glow effect.The bounds are encoded as a Rectangle.To enlarge the bounds, the top and left values should be negative,and the bottom and right values should be positive.This method calls `getPadding()` to get the raw padding values,and uses `Math.ceil()` to set the values of `paddingOverride`and `currentPadding`.

r.x: The rounded padding required by this filter.

m.x: Sets the active state of this filter.A disabled filter will not be used.

p.x: `true` to enable this filter, or `false` to disable it.

m.x: Sets the padding override.If this is set, the filter will use this padding instead of calculating it.Call `setPaddingOverride(null)` to clear the override.Call `setPaddingOverride()` to set the padding to 0.
